t0: Metrics queried with PromQL (also Thanos, Mimir, VictoriaMetrics). The usual choice for error rates and latency.
t1: Logs queried with LogQL: count errors or look for a message after a deployment.
t2: SQL over logs or events kept in ClickHouse.
t3: Searches over logs; the runner lists the only indices pipelines may search.
t4: The same as Elasticsearch, for OpenSearch clusters.
t5: Named statements the runner runs in a read-only transaction, such as counting failed orders.
t6: Named requests to any JSON API, with a path into the answer: a status page or your own health endpoint.
t9: a group of {projects} with shared settings (a team, a department)
t11: The plural, as lists and menus show it.
t12: Labels only: no address, command or file changes with it.
t13: A word (such as guide or flight_plan; add _plural for a plural) and what to call it. The Words page is easier.
t14: People may approve their own runs
t15: Not set: yes without sign-in, no with sign-in
t16: Lets the person who started a run approve it. Off is the safer choice once people sign in: a second person must look.
t17: The role needed on a {project} to run pipeline text from the editor that is not in Git yet. none turns draft runs off.
t18: Draft pipelines are not reviewed; letting them read secrets lets anyone who may start one read them too.
t20: A pull request can change the pipeline; with secrets on, whoever opens one can make a step print them. {Projects} may override this.
t21: Turns every pipeline's schedule triggers on or off. {Projects} may override this.
t22: The role needed on every {project} to make join tokens and to revoke or rotate runners.
t23: The role needed on a {project} to waive one of its policies' rules (on the environment too, for a deploy rule). none turns waivers off.
t24: How long a waiver may last; at most 365.
t25: The longest an API token may last; at most 3650.
t26: How many combinations one loop (a matrix) may have; at most 500.
t28: How many MiB of report files the server accepts for one step attempt; runners are told and send no more. Default 24.
t29: Beyond it, only the totals. Default 50000.
t31: Over all its runs: the oldest runs' results are removed first, keeping their totals. Default 1000000.
t33: SARIF accepted per step attempt. Default 32.
t37: How much of an SBOM is read to summarize it. Default 64.
t38: Files in a step's attachments directory. Default 2000.
t44: The largest file an artifact may hold. Default 1024.
t45: How much one run may keep. Default 4096.
t46: How much a {project} may keep over all its runs. Default 50.
t47: How long artifacts are kept when the pipeline does not say (30d, 2w, 12h).
t48: The longest any artifact is kept, whatever the pipeline says.
t49: Off by default. On, this server hosts Git repositories you can clone, fetch and push over HTTPS, and the repository calls, tools and commands work. Turning it off stops the Git endpoints and keeps the data. Takes effect when each server next restarts.
t50: Used in each repository's clone address. Empty: the address the request came in on.
t51: The owner of a repository made without one.
t53: Off: only a listener on this machine accepts Basic credentials without HTTPS. Turn on only behind something that already encrypts.
t54: The most one repository's packs may total. Default: no limit.
t55: The largest push, request body and pack. Default 2048.
t56: The most repositories one owner may have. Default: no limit.
t57: How fast repositories may be created, in all. Default 60.
t58: The most git processes serving requests at once on a server. Default 32.
t60: How much the repository caches on one server may take; the least recently used are removed. Default: no limit.
t61: How often packs are consolidated, collected and checked. At least 1m.
t62: Off while empty. An address such as :2222 turns on Git over SSH, served by the servers themselves; people add keys under SSH keys. Takes effect when each server next restarts.
t63: The host SSH clone addresses name. Empty: the host of the address clients clone from.
t64: The port SSH clone addresses name; 22 makes them git@host:owner/name.git. Default: the port it listens on.
t65: Public keys, one per line, of the authorities whose user certificates are accepted. The first principal of a certificate is the person's name. Empty: certificates are not accepted.
t66: The most SSH connections at once on a server. Default 256.
t67: The most SSH connections from one address. Default 20.
t68: A connection that moves no bytes for this long is closed. At least 1m.
t69: The longest any SSH connection lasts. At least 1m.
t70: The {organization}'s name as people read it, such as your company's name.
t71: A sentence about it, shown where it helps.
t72: How the {unit} is shown. The name above stays the same in URLs and the command line.
t73: Who it is and what its {projects} are.
t75: The Git repository of templates and scripts. It is fetched with the same credentials as {projects}: the server's own Git settings, never a password typed here.
t77: The Git URL (https:// or SSH) Launchway reads. It uses the server's own Git credentials.
t78: The branch manual runs start from when nobody picks another.
t79: How often Launchway asks the repository for new commits, such as 30s or 2m. A Git webhook can make it look at once.
t81: The library whose template is this {project}'s pipeline, at commits without a .launchway/pipeline.yaml. A file in the repository takes its place.
t82: The template's name in that library.
t83: A tag, branch or full commit id of the library. A tag keeps runs repeatable; a branch follows the library as it changes.
t84: The values the template is given, name=value per line.
t85: Start a run when someone pushes to the repository (to the branches or tags below; none listed: any).
t86: Branch names or patterns that start runs when pushed to.
t87: Tag names or patterns that start runs when pushed.
t88: Start a run for each pull request and each push to it.
t89: A newer run cancels older ones
t90: A new run of a push or pull request cancels the older runs of the same branch that are still going, so only the latest commit uses runners.
t92: Overrides the {installation}'s setting for this {project}. Whoever opens a pull request can change what its steps do.
t94: Editor saves to branches starting with
t95: With this set (or Direct branches), the pipeline editor commits to the repository with the server's credentials. Every save makes a new branch starting with this.
t96: Branch patterns the editor may commit to directly, without a new branch. Default: none.
t97: Lets the {project}'s Git host call a webhook that makes the server look for pushes at once.
t99: The name of the server's environment variable that holds the webhook's secret. The secret itself is never stored here.
t100: Or a file on the server holding it.
t101: What deploy runners serve to reach the environment: in practice, its cluster. A deploy pool lists the targets its runners serve.
t103: Names or patterns such as web-*. A {project} not listed cannot deploy here.
t104: newest: a run waiting for the environment's lock is skipped when a newer run of the same service starts waiting. all: every run deploys in turn.
t105: The person who started a run may not promote its deployment here (unless people may approve their own runs); someone else with the operator role must. Anyone with the operator role here may abort.
t106: A build pool runs the steps of {projects}. A deploy pool does deploy and rollback steps for targets, and nothing else.
t107: Build pools: names or patterns ("*" for all) of the {projects} whose steps its runners take.
t108: Deploy pools: the environments' targets its runners deploy to.
t111: Deploy pools without require_identity: the server's environment variable holding the pool's own token (at least 32 characters). Never the token itself.
t112: Refuses shared tokens: only runners enrolled with a join token for this pool serve it. Recommended: each runner then has its own identity that can be revoked.
t113: A group from your identity provider. Give a group or a user, not both.
t116: viewer reads; operator also starts runs, approves and acts on deployments; admin may also change the configuration.
t118: Limits what the binding grants on deployments (promote, abort and approvals that name a deployment) to these environments. Empty: all.
t119: What the policy is for, at most 500 characters. Shown wherever its verdict is.
t120: enforce stops the step (or the run at its start) when a rule fails; report records and shows a warning and never changes an outcome.
t121: Patterns of the {projects} it governs. Empty: every run.
t122: Only deploy rules may be scoped to environments.
t123: A run without a branch (a tag or a pull request) does not match.
t124: The library whose files hold the policies.
t125: A tag or a full commit id; a branch is refused, so policies change only when you move the version.
t126: Every *.yaml and *.yml file below it is read. Default policies.
t128: How often each server looks at the version again, 10s to 168h.
t129: How long a version loaded earlier is still used while the repository cannot be reached; after that, governed runs fail closed.
t130: What kind of system it is. Where it is and its credentials are set on the deploy runners, which are next to it.
t133: How to talk to the model: the Anthropic Messages API, or OpenAI-compatible chat completions (local model servers among them).
t134: The provider's id of the model, such as claude-sonnet-5-5 or qwen3:8b.
t135: The base URL. Default https://api.anthropic.com for anthropic; required for openai.
t136: Where the key is kept, in a secret store the runners (and the server, to explain failures) have: never the key itself. A local server may need none.
t137: Input plus output. Empty: no limit.
t140: Headers that are not secret, name=value per line.
t141: In cores, such as 8 or 500m. Empty: no limit.
t142: Most memory a step may ask for
t144: Defaults for steps that ask for nothing
t145: Above it the step is slowed, not stopped.
t146: Other kinds of step (image builds and the like) have defaults of their own: set them on the Raw tab under defaults.
t148: The OpenID Connect issuer URL the provider shows for the application.
t149: The application's client id in the provider.
t150: This server's address plus /auth/callback; register exactly it in the provider.
t151: Environment variable that holds the client secret
t152: Only the name is kept here, never the secret: it is set on every server from your secret manager.
t153: The claim the provider puts groups in; groups by default.
t154: Which claim names the person; the default is usually right.
t155: Groups whose members are the first administrators
t156: Group names as the provider sends them.
t157: User names of the first administrators.
t158: What kind of store pipelines may name. Its address and credentials stay with the runners.
t159: Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, at most 63 characters. It cannot be changed later.
t160: What pipelines call it: lower-case letters, digits and hyphens. It cannot be changed later.
t161: tag: a tag or a full commit id; commit: only a full commit id.
t163: host/path patterns: * within one part, a final /** any depth.
t165: 1 to 20; the person who started the run does not count.
